quotes.verbatim_quote:
This convergence system shows a fixed bombardment of
any type chord that we want to give "tonal significance" to then
bombard it with 24 scales, a mixture of them, their ideas and
constituent chords.
quotes.why_load_bearing: This is the foundational definition of the entire method -- the systematic application of 24 scales to any target chord as a means of approaching tonal resolution.

quotes.verbatim_quote:
I conceived this convergence system by using a one chord tag
at the very end of "Stella Bye Starlite." The first chord (numbered)
of each of the following group of 43 chords & scales yield a different
type V chord (function) and its parent scale, yielding several con-
vergent scales & their chords for tonal convergence.
quotes.why_load_bearing: Martino explains exactly how the system was conceived -- each of the 43 chords/scales functions as a unique kind of V chord, giving the player dozens of approach routes to a tonal destination.

quotes.verbatim_quote:
Before playing each scale in this
system, you should brainwash your ear with the
tonality (F major in this case) with several cadences
into the key. (Ex. G-7-C7 FA) (G£-C 139 FA)
I- VI- II- V-T ect.
quotes.why_load_bearing: This is a prescriptive practice rule -- the player must first internalize the destination tonality through cadential repetition before attempting convergent scale approaches.

quotes.verbatim_quote:
When converging on a tonality project yourself sound wise to
it already having your attention (sound attention) on it and

on the chord or scale you are using.
quotes.why_load_bearing: This gives the mental/aural technique that accompanies the physical scale work -- the improviser must simultaneously hear the destination while executing the approach scale.

quotes.verbatim_quote:
Scale #1. A pentatonic scale having a a Dox 7th (of C7 chord)
in it which resolves voice leadingly into the note
A (The vital 3rd of F major). Also contains A
(G-pb ) Tritone which the note pb resolves (as
both of C 7th) To the 5th (C) and the note G re-
solves to F the root note.
quotes.why_load_bearing: Martino's analysis of Scale #1 establishes the template for all subsequent scale justifications -- each note's convergent function into the target key is traced through tritone and voice-leading logic.

quotes.verbatim_quote:
Scale # 4. This scale is a diminish scale on the tonic "C".

It has an interval structure half, whole, half, whole,

half, whole, half, whole. The scale has an E-B Db tri-
tone also a G-D ee giving it a number of con-
vergent factors into major or minor tonality.
quotes.why_load_bearing: This is the first diminished scale entry and establishes the H-W interval structure definition used as a reference point for comparing Scale #5.

quotes.verbatim_quote:
Scale # 5.

This scale is a second type diminish scale. It has

a W,H,W,H,W,H,W,H step symmetry. It permits ascending
diminish color to a point of convergence (F major in
this case). It has the same symmetrical indifference
as the # 4 scale which permits it to be used (starting
on different notes) for converging cadences to several
tonalities.
quotes.why_load_bearing: Distinguishes the W-H diminished scale from the H-W variant and articulates the key property of 'symmetrical indifference' that makes both diminished scales useful across multiple tonal destinations.

quotes.verbatim_quote:
Scale # 6.

This is a Jazz melodic minor scale. It permits a
minor color-quality asendance into tonality (F major)
it is important because of its intervallic symmetry
its D bstarting note, and the different chords it
produces. (G b oan, E+A7, Be nb7 + pb_4~ 7).
quotes.why_load_bearing: Introduces the Jazz melodic minor as a convergent scale type, identifying the characteristic chord it produces and its function as the first of several minor-quality approach scales in the system.

quotes.verbatim_quote:
Scale # 7.

This scale is a major scale with the 4th degree
and 5th degree raised. It contains an E bi3 bs
chord which is the sound of all the scale notes
sounded together simultaneously.
quotes.why_load_bearing: Defines the raised-4th-and-5th major scale type and introduces the technique of stacking all scale tones simultaneously to identify a scale's characteristic chord sound.

quotes.verbatim_quote:
Scale # 10.

This scale is the whole tone scale cb), It has its
perfect whole, bold steps which leads also into F
major. The linking chord is the cb7 bs which resolves
nicely into F major. Other chords which have resolving
tendencies are the C+7, ¢ 69411, c7b 5.
quotes.why_load_bearing: Introduces the whole tone scale as a convergent type, names its characteristic 'linking chord,' and lists the family of chords the scale produces for tonal approach.

quotes.verbatim_quote:
Extract all possible chords from all scales for

resolution purposes.
quotes.why_load_bearing: This is a direct, universally applicable practice instruction -- every scale in the system should be mined for its constituent chords, each of which can independently serve as a convergent device.

quotes.topic: System purpose -- color and route variety
quotes.verbatim_quote:
Remember this system is about how to get into a major or minor

key variating different scales (24) and chords (many) and their

innumerable permutation & chord inversions.
quotes.why_load_bearing: Martino restates the system's core pedagogical goal in a single sentence, clarifying that the 24 scales are not ends in themselves but tools for multiplying approach routes to any tonal destination.
